### Reproduction

```python
from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModelForCausalLM

MODEL = "google/gemma-3-1b-it"
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(MODEL)
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(MODEL)
print(tokenizer.eos_token_id) # 1
print(model.config.eos_token_id) # [1, 106]
```

### Expected behavior

## Expected Behavior

Tokenizer and Model Config should be consistent on eos_token_id so that the following generation loop can work correctly:
```python
for _ in range(max_new_tokens):
    ...
    if new_token_id.item() == tokenizer.eos_token_id:
        break  # should break the loop
```

comments.body:
This is expected behavior, not a bug.  

### We have two EOS tokens for instruction-tuned models

- `token 1` is `<eos>`  :  the standard end-of-sequence token.                                                          
- `token 106` is `<end_of_turn>` :  a special token added by the chat template for instruction-tuned models   
                                                                                                  
    
### Why we have two EOS tokens?
                               
  During model conversion ([convert_gemma3_weights.py](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/aa1c36f1a9f454e69c4eac83071ced235942c7ed/src/transformers/models/gemma3/convert_gemma3_weights.py):608-611), 

when a chat template is included (for instruction-tuned (ends with '-it' variants), the config is explicitly set to:                                                          
  ```python                                                                                                               
# Chat template is included for instruction tuned models, which treat                                                  
# both "<eos>" and "<end_of_turn>" as generation stoppers.                                                             
config.eos_token_id = [1, 106]                                                                                         
  ```                                                                                                             
  So google/gemma-3-1b-it's config gets [1, 106] because the model should stop on either token. The tokenizer only       
  exposes a single eos_token_id because it doesn't know about chat-template-level stop tokens.                           
                                                                                                                                                                            
so, when you do,
```python
if new_token_id.item() == tokenizer.eos_token_id:  # only checks token 1                                               
    break                                                                                                              
 ```
you miss the <end_of_turn> (106). 

The correct check when doing manual generation loops is check against the model's config (handles all stop tokens)    

```python                                             
eos_ids = model.config.eos_token_id                                                                                    
if isinstance(eos_ids, int):                                                                                           
    eos_ids = [eos_ids]                                                                                                
if new_token_id.item() in eos_ids:                                                                                     
    break                                                                                                              
```

  Or you can simply use model.generate() which handles this automatically.   
                                                                                                                         
  TL;DR         

| | Value | reason |
|---|---|---|
|tokenizer.eos_token_id | 1 |Only knows about <eos> |
| model.config.eos_token_id | [1, 106] |Includes <end_of_turn> for chat models |

title: [Gemma-3] Inconsistent eos_token_id configuration: tokenizer has single value (1) but model.config has list [1, 106]
